We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need propose route using templates. We have target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We can think disconnections: amide bond between aniline (methoxy phenyl amine) and heterocycle carboxamide. So step 1: form amide coupling of 4-methoxyaniline (or 4-methoxy-? Actually the aniline is attached to phenyl ring at para? SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)... )c1. That's anisidine (4-methoxyaniline). So we can get anisidine commercially (price ~50). Then need acyl chloride or activated acid of heterocycle: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N with carbonyl attached (carboxamide). The heterocycle is a 1,2,4-triazine? Actually c2nnn(... )c2N is a 1,2,4-triazine? The carbonyl attached to N? The SMILES: NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So it's a diaminotriazine with a side chain phenyl-CH2-N-azetidine? Actually CN4CC(F)C4 is a fluorinated azetidine? It's a 4-membered ring with F. So we can think disconnection at the C-CH2-aryl bond linking triazine to phenyl. So step 2: attach phenyl-CH2-... to triazine via SNAr? The triazine has a C attached to phenyl via CH2 (alkyl). Could be formed via alkylation of triazine with benzyl halide. So we could have triazine core with N-H groups (maybe 2,4-diamino-1,3,5-triazin-2-one?). Actually we have c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N: a 1,2,4-triazine ring with an N-substituted side chain (benzyl). So we can start from 2,4-diamino-1,3,5-triazine (or similar) and do N-alkylation with benzyl bromide bearing the side chain (para-aminomethyl? Actually the side chain is phenyl-CH2-N-azetidine). So we need benzyl bromide with that side chain: (4-(N-azetidinyl)phenyl)methyl bromide. That could be made from 4-(N-azetidinyl)benzyl alcohol then convert to bromide. Or we could start from 4-(N-azetidinyl)benzyl bromide commercially? Probably not.

Alternative: disconnection at the azetidine side chain: we could have 4-(chloromethyl)phenyl attached to azetidine via nucleophilic substitution (SN2) of azetidine amine onto benzyl chloride. So step: make 4-(chloromethyl)phenyl attached to triazine? Wait the side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3: a phenyl attached via CH2 to N of azetidine. So the phenyl is attached to triazine via CH2 (benzyl). So we could first make benzyl chloride (or bromide) attached to phenyl with N-azetidine substituent already present? Actually the phenyl has a substituent CN4CC(F)C4 (i.e., CH2 attached to N of azetidine). So the phenyl is para-substituted with CH2-N-azetidine. So we could start from 4-(azetidin-1-ylmethyl)phenyl bromide (or chloride). That could be made by reacting 4-bromomethylbenzene with azetidine (nucleophilic substitution). Azetidine with fluorine? The azetidine is N-? Actually CN4CC(F)C4: N attached to CH2 which attaches to phenyl, and the azetidine ring has a fluorine on carbon. So the azetidine is 4-fluoroazetidine (maybe 3-fluoro?). So we need 4-fluoroazetidine commercially? Search.
